evals.name: check-is-read-only
evals.expected_output: The current effective configuration is reported — each key with the layer supplying it (user-global, team, local overlay), absent layers named, drift flagged (unknown keys, dead globs, unsupported em-dash threshold) — and no file is written.
expectations: Reports the effective config per key with the winning layer named
Flags drift such as unknown keys or an unsupported em-dash threshold key

evals.name: apply-writes-team-layer-only-with-confirmation
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup apply — user asks to exempt docs/style-guide.md from the em-dash rule
evals.expected_output: A diff of .claude/ai-slop.json adding docs/style-guide.md to em_dash_allowed_paths is shown and explicitly confirmed before writing. The user-global and .local.json layers are named as self-service options, never written by the skill.
expectations: Shows the proposed team-layer diff and waits for explicit confirmation before writing
Writes ONLY .claude/ai-slop.json, never the user-global or local overlay layers
Adds the exemption under em_dash_allowed_paths rather than excluded_paths (the file should still be scanned by other rules)

evals.name: em-dash-default-posture-holds
evals.prompt: /ai-slop:setup apply — user asks to raise the em-dash threshold repo-wide
evals.expected_output: The skill explains the em-dash rule is zero-tolerance by design with per-document exemption as the supported mechanism, offers em_dash_allowed_paths for the documents that genuinely need em dashes, and does not invent a threshold key for the rule.
expectations: Explains the zero-tolerance default and that exemption is per-document, not per-threshold
Offers em_dash_allowed_paths (or disabled_rules with its trade-off named) as the supported paths
Does not write a nonexistent em-dash threshold key
